killing_reference.title: Antimicrobial and antifouling conformal hydrogel coatings
killing_elements: D: polymer selected from agar, chitosan, N-isopropylacrylamide copolymer, poloxamer, poly(ethylene oxide)/poly(lactic acid) block copolymer, poly(ethylene oxide)/poly(propylene oxide) block copolymers, alginate, dextran, and copolymers thereof
killing_relationships: the aqueous pre-hydrogel solution comprises a mixture of a monomer with antimicrobial activity, a monomer with antifouling activity, and a polymer
the mixture when polymerized together forms a hydrogel
the coated substrate is contacted with a swelling agent
the non-conformal hydrogel coating is removed from the coated substrate
killing_reference.killing_arrangement: The aqueous pre-hydrogel solution is applied to a substrate, then polymerized, and the non-conformal hydrogel coating is removed, leaving the conformal hydrogel coating on the substrate.
killing_reference.what_was_already_disclosed: The prior art already teaches: a substrate having a conformal hydrogel coating prepared by applying an aqueous pre-hydrogel solution comprising a mixture of a monomer with antimicrobial activity, a monomer with antifouling activity, and a polymer, polymerizing the solution, contacting the coated substrate with a swelling agent, and removing the non-conformal hydrogel coating.

commercial_objective.customer_problem: The buyer (likely a medical device manufacturer or a researcher) faces the challenge of creating a hydrogel coating with improved mechanical strength and resistance to polymer chain scission, which can be a limitation in various applications such as wound dressings, contact lenses, or biosensors.
commercial_objective.economic_value_hypothesis: The invention would create economic value by enabling the development of more durable and reliable hydrogel-based products, reducing the need for frequent replacements and minimizing the risk of product failure, which can lead to cost savings and improved patient outcomes.
commercial_objective.desired_technical_effect: The desired technical effect is a hydrogel coating with enhanced mechanical strength and reduced susceptibility to polymer chain scission, achieved through the reinforcement of the hydrogel matrix with nanofibers.

architecture_alternatives.description: The hydrogel matrix is reinforced with nanofibers that are covalently bonded to the hydrogel matrix through a click reaction, creating a stronger and more stable interface.
architecture_alternatives.material_difference: The click reaction creates a covalent bond between the nanofibers and the hydrogel matrix, which is more stable than the non-covalent interactions in the prior art.
architecture_alternatives.new_technical_effect: The covalent bond between the nanofibers and the hydrogel matrix enhances the mechanical strength and reduces the impact of polymer chain scission.
architecture_alternatives.commercial_value_note: The improved mechanical strength and reduced susceptibility to polymer chain scission preserve the commercial value of the hydrogel coating in various applications such as wound dressings, contact lenses, or biosensors.

architecture_alternatives.description: The hydrogel coating is prepared under high-pressure conditions, which induces the formation of a more ordered and stable hydrogel structure.
architecture_alternatives.material_difference: The high-pressure conditions create a more ordered and stable hydrogel structure, which is more resistant to polymer chain scission.
architecture_alternatives.new_technical_effect: The more ordered and stable hydrogel structure enhances the mechanical strength and reduces the impact of polymer chain scission.
architecture_alternatives.commercial_value_note: The improved mechanical strength and reduced susceptibility to polymer chain scission preserve the commercial value of the hydrogel coating in various applications such as wound dressings, contact lenses, or biosensors.
